title: Always owing the record company and signing without advice
summary: She says artists never get out of debt to record companies and she, like others, signed without managers or lawyers.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: You made a very interesting point today, before we were talking on tape, when you said that you have an indication that you must be selling records somewhere from your ASCAP royalties, yet you never get any report of this from record companies.
No, no. The record companies, you

always owe the record company. You owe them all the time. You never get out of debt with the record company. Well, this was a bad scene to start with, because years ago, you know -- see today, when they get an artist today, or get kids recording today, well, they put out an awful lot of cash money, you know, to the kids, or to the managers. Well, these kids are smart enough to have managers and lawyers and blah, blah, blah. Well, unfortunately I, like the most of us, didn't have that, when we started recording, you know. So somebody was smart enough to cap on this, you see. Which was an unfair thing, but I suppose when it comes down to a business type of thing, this is what they're looking at, you see. And of course many people are very anxious to get into the thing. They don't take the time to ask questions you know, about anything. My God, if somebody says, "I'm interested in you," blah, blah, "I'd like to put you on records." Well, they're so thrilled at the idea. Nowadays I don't do that. I learned the lesson the hard way, you see. So anytime I'm doing anything today I want to know what it's all about, you know.

But I'm just saying that at that time the average person didn't -- you didn't bother about talking to a lawyer about this, should I do this, or what terms should I ask for, or should I accept this under these terms. You just didn't do that, you see. And you were taken advantage of.
